candidate.title: Embodied RAG and non-parametric Memory
candidate.description:
This new AI research paper by Carnegie Mellon University introduces Embodied-RAG, a novel framework that extends Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to the domain of embodied agents, such as robots, enabling them to autonomously construct and utilize hierarchical, non-parametric memory systems. 

This NEW framework addresses the unique challenges of applying RAG to embodied experiences, which involve multimodal data, high spatial and temporal correlations, and the necessity for varying levels of abstraction in perception. Embodied-RAG enhances foundational models by integrating a semantic forest—a hierarchical organization of language descriptions at multiple levels of detail—with a topological map for navigation, allowing efficient retrieval and context-sensitive generation across different robotic platforms.

The memory construction process involves building a topological map that captures spatial information and observations, and organizing these observations into a hierarchical semantic forest through agglomerative clustering based on spatial proximity. 

Each node in the semantic forest represents a different level of abstraction, from specific object arrangements (leaf nodes) to global environmental summaries (root nodes). During retrieval, the framework employs a language model to traverse the semantic forest, selecting relevant nodes based on the query, and effectively aligning the query's abstraction level with the appropriate memory resolution. This retrieval mechanism mitigates perceptual hallucinations common in naive RAG applications by incorporating robust reasoning over the hierarchical structure.

The framework shows significant improvements in handling implicit queries, generating accurate global summaries, and providing robust navigation and explanation capabilities. By effectively addressing the challenges of applying non-parametric memory to embodied agents, Embodied-RAG presents a promising general-purpose system capable of task-, environment-, and platform-agnostic operation, enhancing the ability of robots to navigate and communicate effectively in complex, real-world scenarios.
